source_photo_support: The Purdue exterior photograph and Indiana Architect Oct 1965 p.32 show long, slender, vertically continuous dark glazing with fine floor-level divisions, separated by broad pale piers.
edits: Applied photo-supported narrow continuous upper-storey glazed slots to the long visible elevations (8–10 bays), not just two selected runs; retained per-floor windows on short return/entrance faces.
Used a 0.04 m sill and transoms 0.04 m above slab tops so the continuous glass remains visible between the modeled 0.30 m slab edges instead of reading as disconnected squat windows.
Slot width remains a visual estimate of 0.82 m; no photo supplies measured dimensions.
Retained all footprint, roof/floor elevations, entry, courtyard seam, interior and master placement geometry.
uncertainties: The perspective sources do not provide measured bay widths; 0.82 m glazing and 0.72 m piers are visual proportions, not surveyed dimensions.
The photos support this cadence only on visible elevations; hidden/re-entrant face details remain uncertain.
Courtyard/re-entrant gap and roof/penthouse levels remain unchanged and unverified.
